title: Inherent's Faraday research agent and its Anthropic/OpenAI benchmark claim
reason: Verified AND falsified now (cycle 2 verifier + cycle 3 adversarial falsifier, both fresh contexts) -- ran out of cycle time twice before drafting/editor gate, carried forward as a ready candidate, not a gate failure. Findings: Inherent (London, DeepMind-alumni-founded AI lab) raised a $50M seed round (Index Ventures + Radical Ventures co-led, closed 2026-05-29/31), confirmed well beyond the 2-independent-source bar (tech.eu, UKTN, Index Ventures' own post, TechCrunch, 9+ outlets total). Separately, Inherent has its OWN Tier-0 primary source for the agent's existence/launch: https://inherentlabs.ai/research/training-to-replicate (2026-08-14) plus a companion paper, arXiv:2608.13331 (submitted 2026-08-13, 11 named authors) -- this confirms the 'Faraday agent exists and was released' announcement claim on its own, separate from funding. The company's claim that Faraday outperforms Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 at replicating published research findings remains Inherent's own self-designed/self-administered benchmark ('Replica', 310 tasks/100 papers, judged by Inherent's own LLM judge + human study) -- cycle 3's falsifier searched specifically for independent evaluation (METR, Vals AI, Artificial Analysis, academic replication) and found none; must be published, if at all, as an explicit vendor-claim. Nuance for drafting: Faraday's core is Qwen3.6-27B but it calls out to OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Codex as a subordinate coding tool within its own pipeline, so a bare 'tiny model beats giant models' framing overstates it -- scope precisely. No contradiction, denial, or debunking found by either pass. dedup-check clean (no matches) as of cycle 2.
watch: Any independent third-party evaluation (METR or similar) of the Faraday/Replica benchmark
A second outlet with its own reporting on the Anthropic/OpenAI comparison claim
